borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
description: Change of use of the dwelling (Use Class C3) to an HMO for 6 persons (Use Class C4)
decision_conditions: <p>The proposed development would result in the loss of two family-sized dwellinghouses, the need for which is clearly demonstrated in the development plan and supporting evidence base. While it would provide a dwelling in the form of an HMO, it fails to demonstrate that this meets an identified need and would not present a suitable quality of accommodation specifically for an HMO. Additionally, the development site is not located within an area of high access to public transport and is therefore not considered an appropriate location for an HMO. As such, the proposal is considered to have a detrimental impact on the borough's housing supply and is contrary to the following policies:&nbsp;</p><p>- National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)</p><p>-&nbsp;Policies D6 and H9 of the London Plan (March 2021)</p><p>-&nbsp;Policies DMH5 and SP3 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</p>

<p>The proposed development fails to demonstrate&nbsp;that additional demand for parking from the development could be adequately accommodated in the surrounding area. The proposal is therefore likely to add unacceptably to parking stress and congestion in the vicinity of the application site,&nbsp;<span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt;">resulting from&nbsp;an increase in the number of households residing at the site as well as the loss of 1x off-street parking space</span>.&nbsp; As such, it fails to comply with the following policies&nbsp;which seek to ensure proposals show how car parking will be designed and managed and to take into consideration on-street parking availability and existing and planned public transport provision:</p><p>National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)</p><p>Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)</p><p>Policies DMT1 and&nbsp;DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)</p>
